chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said regarding the compurgation (sworn endorsements): fifty men for the deliberate [killing], and for the erroneous [killing], twenty-five men, and upon them is that they should swear by Allah.

key_terms.الْخَطَإِ: Error; accidental action, specifically referring to accidental homicide
key_terms.الْعَمْدِ: Deliberate; intentional action, specifically referring to deliberate homicide in this context
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: Compurgation; a ritual of sworn oaths by a group of men to establish evidence in homicide cases
key_terms.يَحْلِفُوا: They should swear; the act of taking oaths by the group of men

ai.seo_question: How many men are required for compurgation in deliberate versus accidental homicide according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific numerical requirements for qasamah, a mechanism where a group of men swear oaths to identify the killer in cases of homicide where the perpetrator is unknown. It distinguishes between deliberate murder, requiring fifty men, and accidental killing, requiring twenty-five, reflecting the jurisprudential principle that the severity of the crime correlates with the number of witnesses needed to establish the presumption of guilt. This ruling is central to Shia fiqh regarding blood money (diya) and the transfer of liability when the killer remains unidentified.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the compurgation (sworn endorsements) being fifty men regarding the deliberate (killing), and regarding the erroneous, being twenty-five men, and upon them is that they should be swearing by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
